subject: E2E response envelope clarification & demo assets
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@altonanalytics.com>, Lydia Park <lpark@altonanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: E2E response envelope clarification & demo assets

Hi Samir / Lydia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so engineering has a single place to reason about the p95/p99 acceptance criteria for the hosted evaluation vs your current provider.

What we covered:
- Baseline ask: end-to-end (client -> Redwood hosted API -> model -> response) p95 and p99 targets for your real traffic. You said target p95 <= 220ms and p99 <= 420ms for 75% of traffic, with occasional spikes allowed.
- Streaming: you will test both streaming and non-streaming paths; streaming needs to support chunk delivery latency per-token p95 <= 45ms.
- Concurrency and throughput: initial POC load expected 250 req/s with 6 concurrent long-running streams (average 6s).
- Failure modes: we discussed model fallback to smaller quantized variant and region failover.

Deliverables I will provide (attached):
- redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx: mapping of p95/p99 buckets, traffic envelopes, and suggested configs (batch sizes, max inflight, kv cache warmup).
- demo recording: short export of today’s live run (link in Drive).
- traffic-envelope-sample.json: suggested synthetic traffic profile you can run to reproduce the envelope.

Asks for Alton to confirm before we schedule the evaluation run:
1) Please confirm the p95/p99 numeric targets you want us to gate on (those above or revised).
2) Confirm whether payload sizes for this workload are uniformly ~1–1.5KB or if you have a fat-tail of >5KB inputs (impacts kernel selection & batching).
3) Provide a single Vault/KMS domain we can use for test telemetry (or confirm we should use pseudonymized tokens).

Next steps: once you confirm (1–3) we’ll propose a 48-hour shadow run window and provide a runbook with acceptance checks and rollback criteria.

Thanks —

Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), demo-recording-20261207.mp4 (video), traffic-envelope-sample.json (json)
From: Samir Shah <samir@altonanalytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Park <lpark@altonanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T17:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: E2E response envelope clarification & demo assets

Logan —

Appreciate the recap and the files. A few clarifications from our side before we lock in a shadow run:

- Targets: the engineering team is comfortable with p95 <= 240ms and p99 <= 480ms for the initial evaluation. If Redwood can hit p95 <= 220ms that's a huge plus, but the above are the acceptance thresholds we’ll grade against.
- Payloads: ~88% of requests are ~1.2KB; we have a 12% fat-tail where inputs spike to 6–12KB (long transcripts). We'll flag them in the envelope and are happy for Redwood to exclude the top 2% if needed for parity testing.
- Streaming: token emission constraints matter — we need per-chunk p95 <= 60ms (we're ok increasing from the 45ms you mentioned if it materially helps batching).
- Concurrency: the 250 req/s is correct for the POC. During business hours we see sustained 200–300rps. The six concurrent long streams was our average; peaks hit ~18 concurrent long streams for a 30m window.

One more ask: do you have a suggested traffic shaping configuration we should pre-provision to better match our production envelope (burst buckets, token limits)? If you can share that before the run we’ll implement it in our load harness.

Thanks —
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
Alton Analytics
samir@altonanalytics.com

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the detailed traffic notes, that helps a lot. A couple of technical clarifications and the runbook outline we’ll use:

1) Acceptance thresholds we’ll gate:
   - p95 (end-to-end): pass if <= 240ms under the agreed traffic envelope.
   - p99 (end-to-end): pass if <= 480ms with exception handling for the top 2% heaviest payloads (per Samir’s note).
   - streaming chunk emission: p95 <= 60ms per chunk.

2) Traffic shaping recommendation (we’ll send a sample jmeter/locust config):
   - Baseline sustained: 200 rps for 90% of test window.
   - Burst policy: 25% burst headroom for 10-minute windows (simulate the observed peaks).
   - Long-stream channel: reserve 20 concurrent stream slots during peak windows; allow autoscale to 35 for 5-minute bursts.

3) Batching & kernel guidance:
   - For your 1–1.5KB common payloads we recommend batch_target=16 with max_latency_ms=12.
   - For fat-tail >5KB traffic, use a separate route with batch_target=4 to avoid head-of-line latency.

4) Observability and pass/fail checks we’ll capture during the run:
   - Token-level latency breakdown (network hop, model, tokenization, post-process).
   - Percentile plots (p50/p95/p99) and tail-sampling traces for any request above p99 threshold.
   - Canary fallback: if p99 > 650ms for 10 consecutive minutes, automatically route to quantized variant and notify both sides.

Proposed schedule:
- Thu 2026-12-10 10:00–14:00 PT: 4-hour shadow run (we’ll provision staging capacity in us-west).
- Pre-run: Wed 2026-12-09 16:00 PT — Redwood will push the traffic shaping config and a sample load job and we’ll validate it with your harness.

Ben, Logan — can you confirm capacity and the runbook link? Samir/Lydia — confirm the schedule above or propose an alternate window.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Performance | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Confirmed on Redwood side: we’ll reserve the capacity for Thu 12/10 10:00–14:00 PT and stand up the shadow pool in us-west-2. A few operational notes:
- We will capture p95/p99 on the full end-to-end path and stream-chunk emit times.
- We’ll provide a live dashboard link during the run and a post-run artifacts bundle (CSV + traces).
- Escalation path: if we see sustained p99 degradation > 480ms we’ll trigger canary fallback and open a shared Zoom.
